channel.title: Naked Itchy Feet
channel.description: Around the world with Kelvin & Priscila - mischief afoot

item.title: Photo album: São Paulo
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: A few days in Brazil's most populous city visiting family and friends and the chance to see their final victory of the World Cup.

item.title: Photo album: Olinda
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: A day wandering around the beautiful old town of Olinda - famous for it's colourful buildings and local artisans.

item.title: Photo album: Canoa Quebrada
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Paragliders, stunning beaches and another victory for Brazil in Canoa Quebrada.

item.title: Photo album: Jericoacoara
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Sand dunes, capoeira, beaches and a mystery fever in the ever-popular Jericoacoara.

item.title: Photo album: Lençois Maranhenses
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
In the north of Brazil lies "the bedsheets" - an expanse of spectacular sand dunes.
After the rainy season the dips in the dunes fill with water to form hundreds of deliciously refreshing swimming pools.

item.title: Photo album: Ilha de Marajó
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
Marajó is an island at the mouth of the Amazon river - the largest fluvial island in the world. With golden sands and mud streets where buffalos roam freely.
A welcome escape from Belém and a great place to see the opening match of the World Cup!

item.title: An unexpected change of plan
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: After over a year on the road we arrived in Brazil ready to slow down our travelling wheels. And we did - but not as planned - with ultrasounds, an epidural, surgery and even pregnancy tests culminating with a drastic change to our Brazilian dream.

item.title: Photo album: Belém
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Longer than planned mostly dealing with doctors and hospitals in the in the North Brazilian city of Belém

item.title: Photo album: Manaus
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Sitting half way down the Amazon river, Manaus is the capital of Amazonia. After four days on a boat we were glad to set foot on land and explore its city streets, beaches and beautiful opera house.

item.title: Photo album: Boat down the Amazon
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Four days sleeping in a hammock on a boat down the Amazon river from Tabatinga at the Colombian border to Manaus.

item.title: Cruising the Galapagos Islands
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Going to the Galapagos Islands had never featured in our immediate travel plans, so it was very unexpectedly that it became one of the highlights of our year around the world. Kelvin's mum, Carol, decided to celebrate her 60th birthday doing something memorable and a cruise through the islands sounded like that sort of thing. It was also an invitation (and privilege) we couldn't refuse.

item.title: One year on the road
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: On the 16th April 2013 we set off from Heathrow with a very vague plan and some date-changeable intercontinental flights. Today, one year later*, we are in the Galapagos Islands looking back over a full year.

item.title: Photo album: South Colombia
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
After Bogota we only had a week to get to Ecuador and see all the highlights on the way. The first stop was the smallest desert we have ever seen - El Deserto de Tatacoa - where we learned about the Southern Hemisphere night sky.
In San Augustin we found a real friendly Colombian small town where an ancient civilisation left a mysterious legacy.
Then we headed towards Mocoa's lush wet jungle and took the "trampoline of death" towards the border with Ecuador where we slept the night at a hotel run by nuns next to the amazing Santuário de Las Lajas - a church built on a bridge over a deep canyon.

item.title: Photo album: Bogota
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
Our South American journey started in Bogota, the capital of Colombia.
We enjoyed the cool climate, street art and colonial feel by foot, cable car and on two wheels. And had our first proper South American steak!

item.title: Photo album: La la land
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: A flying visit to the City of Angels was a great chance to catch up with old friends.

item.title: Photo album: O'ahu
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: From Waikiki to the big surf of the North Shore and the empty beaches of the west coast, O'ahu has something for everyone.

item.title: Photo album: Kaua'i
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
Kaua'i is known as "the garden isle" and is one of the oldest of the Hawaiian islands.
We visited the Na Pali Coast, Waimea Canyon and surfed the waves of Hanalei Bay.

item.title: Support Brazilians at the World Cup
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: In just a few months, Brazil will host the next World Cup. While this is really exciting for football fans around the globe and for Brazil's tourism industry, the costs of hosting the event will leave Brazilian tax payers with a sky high bill to pay. As it stands, the government has already blown the budget, and isn't even close to delivering the infrastructure initially promised to outlive the Cup as a legacy.

item.title: Photo album: The Tongariro Crossing
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: The Tongariro Crossing is said by many to be the best day walk in NZ and maybe even the world... 20 kilometers across a crazy moonscape between volcanoes and lakes. And a side trip up Mount Doom aka Mount Ngauruhoe!

item.title: Photo album: Wellington & Taranaki
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: We passed back through Wellington and caught the start of the rugby sevens and then headed up to the Taranaki Peninsula to see the surf, the mountain and the clouds.

item.title: Photo album: Kaikoura
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description:
More stunning NZ landscapes... Mountains right down to the sea!
And **swimming with dolphins**!

item.title: A stolen glance at Fiji
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Fiji surprised me in many ways. The warmth of the people, the beauty of the landscapes and how these people are so proud of their country are all reasons why it was so easy to fall in love with the place. But Fiji has many egos and can be many different things to those who visit. Even to those who live in it.

item.title: Photo album: Fiji
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: A week in paradise. In cyclone season!

item.title: Photo album: Albany to Esperance
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Stunning white sand beaches with turquoise waters made this one of the most beautiful parts of Australia for us.

item.title: Photo album: Australia - The South West
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Cafe culture and skyscrapers in Perth, surf and vineyards in Margaret River, a terrifying climb up a 70 meter tree and then more surf in Denmark!

item.title: Photo album: Back to Lombok
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: A quick trip back to Lombok to refresh our Australian visas.

item.title: Photo album: Australia - The West Coast
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: From Exmouth down to Perth - sand, sun and surf!

item.title: Western Australia - Lake Argyll to Exmouth
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: After a few hundreds of kilometers on the road, the Northern Territory border with Western Australia slowly approached. The scenery was vast - full of space, freedom and magic colours.

item.title: Photo album: Australia - The North West
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: We crossed over the border into Western Australia and visited Lake Argyll - the campsite with an amazing infinity pool. Then on to Broome then Karijini National Park...

item.title: Photo album: Australia - The Top End
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: In the first fortnight in Australia we saw crocodiles, waterfalls, sunsets, gorges, termite mounds and desert roads in "the top end".

item.title: Aussie Beginnings
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Choosing Darwin as our point of entry into Australia wasn't extensively thought through. The idea started (and ended) with a cheap flight from Bali, ignoring how far Darwin is from anything else in Australia. In fact, we had ignored how far everything is from anything in Australia

item.title: Photo album: Bali - Ubud & the Bukit Peninsula
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Monkeys and dance in Ubud, the incredible surf of the Bukit Peninsula and a visit to the bamboo buildings of the green school.

item.title: Photo album: Bali - Tianyar & Sidemen
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Two weeks teaching English at Yayasan Widya Sari in northern Bali and a weekend trip to Sidemen

item.title: Sun Worship photo challenge
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: We recently found out that Lonely Planet runs a weekly photo challenge on Flickr and we're proud to say that our first entry - into the "Sun Worship" challenge - was awarded joint third place.

item.title: Photo album: Gili Islands
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: After climbing a volcano some serious relaxation was called for and the Gili Islands were just the place...

item.title: Photo album: Rinjani
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: At 3,726 meters high, Rinjani towers over the island of Lombok, Indonesia. For some crazy reason we decided to celebrate Kelvin's birthday by spending three days and two nights climbing it!

item.title: Guidebooks - a modern take
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: The problem with guide books is having to carry them around… And that they are always out of date by the time you are using them… And that the further off the beaten path you get, the less use they are… But mostly having to carry them around! We came up with a few different ways to ease the pain.

item.title: Photo album: Sengiggi
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Our first stop in Lombok was Sengiggi where we were lucky enough to catch the annual "Festival Sengiggi" - a celebration of traditional costumes and dances.

item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Flores' beauty is exciting. When the Portuguese got here in the 15th century they called the island Cabo das Flores (meaning Cape of Flowers) due to its luscious green landscape.

item.title: Adventures on Pelni
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Most tourists choose to travel between Sulawesi and Flores by air for the obvious reasons of speed and convenience with flights scheduled everyday. Most Indonesians however travel by ferry in economy class at a fraction of the cost of a flight. The journey takes 2o hours and there is only one ferry every two weeks so no wonder not many travellers choose this alternative - it takes some organising and timing.

item.title: Death as a way of living in Tana Toraja
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: An equatorial Switzerland, Tana Toraja is the mountainous heart of Sulawesi. It allows for vertiginous views across the valleys and bright green rice paddies fill the landscape creating stairways for giants to touch the heavens. And it is heaven that brings us here, or Torajan's interpretation of it. We are going to a funeral.

item.title: Air BnB in Bangkok
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Like many long term travellers in South East Asia, Bangkok has become a kind of base for us. Whether for vaccinations, visiting dentists or getting visas for the next destination we have spent quite a bit of time in the city. On our last visit we discovered a different way to stay…

item.title: Getting a Myanmar visa in Bangkok
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Our decision to visit Myanmar was a bit last minute and we were already in Thailand so we needed to get our hands on a Myanmar visa whilst in Bangkok. This turned out to be pretty easy but we did have to do a bit of searching around to find out how to get to the embassy and what we needed to bring. Hopefully the information below will help others out...

item.title: Bangkok in May
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: Bangkok in May is hot, and I mean very hot, too hot to do anything. You won't have much fun if your plan is to get lots of sightseeing done.

item.title: Travel Money
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: The days when taking money abroad with you meant travellers cheques or wads of cash are long gone. If you are heading on a long trip is still definitely pays to do your research before you set off though so that you aren't loosing money with every transaction.

item.title: What's the plan?
item.dc:creator: Priscila Santos
item.description: What is our plan? There isn't one really...but thats how travelling is best done, right? Just wander around and see beautiful places, weird cultures, and go where the wind blows us. We have a rough itinerary booked consisting of a few intercontinental flights - and we can change the dates of those so nothing is set in stone.

item.title: Photo album: Kuta Lombok
item.dc:creator: Kelvin Luck
item.description: Kuta is a small laid back surf town on the south coast of Lombok surrounded by some of the most beautiful bays and beaches in Indonesia.
